A dynamic Sales, Packaging & Insurance Professional | Business Development & Market Expansion Strategist

5mo • 

Ever notice how we keep saying “sales is the engine of growth,” and then proceed to overload the engine until it overheats?

We hand our sales teams more tools, more dashboards, more admin, more meetings, more “quick updates,” more CRM fields, more internal requests, more reports about reports… and then we ask:

“Why aren’t we closing more deals?”

Here is a spontaneous thought:
Maybe the problem is not effort. Maybe it is overload.

Salespeople are at their best when they are:
✨ Talking to customers
✨ Understanding real problems
✨ Building trust
✨ Moving opportunities forward

Not when they are drowning in internal noise.

Somewhere along the way, we confused supporting sales with adding layers around sales.

Every new initiative sounds reasonable:
	•	“It will just take 10 minutes.”
	•	“It is important for visibility.”
	•	“We need better tracking.”
	•	“This will help performance.”

Individually? Fine.
Collectively? Heavy.

And here is the part we do not say out loud:
When sales teams feel overloaded, they do not just slow down, they disengage. Creativity drops. Energy fades. Conversations become transactional instead of consultative.

But when you protect their time?
Magic happens.

They prepare better.
They listen deeper.
They follow up sharper.
They close stronger.

So maybe the next time we think about adding “just one more thing,” we pause and ask:

👉 Does this help them sell or just help us feel organized?

If we truly believe sales drives growth, then our job is not to add weight.

It is to remove friction.

Let us stop overwhelming the very people we depend on to create momentum.

Less noise.
More focus.
Real results.

#SalesLeadership #RevenueGrowth #Enablement #FocusOnWhatMatters
